turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
Why am I here? Owen's essay got a zero, and nobody called me first.
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Ms. Kalinowski is fine. Who decided on the zero?
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
Times with no date, no source, no name on them. Show me the page. And you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
I'm not here for jokes. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
Students misquote plays every year, and a wrong line is a wrong line. Show me the page with it on, and the play to check it against. Then tell me who decided on the zero.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
A student changes his argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Show me both pages, dated, side by side.
And the school checker says 94%.
That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to rely on it alone. Your own procedure says the same. Now, the outline and the quotation, on paper.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Flattery isn't evidence. I'm still waiting on the outline and the quotation, on paper.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
There's no moderator in this room, Hale. The outline and the quotation. On paper.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
I'm not here to advise you on your job. I'm here about Owen's essay. Where is the outline?
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? A scoresheet. Owen's essay, Hale.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
You were about to put the outline and the quotation in front of me. Then the zero comes off.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
That's 4.4, and nothing on his record, in writing. But a rewrite for what? You've shown me nothing I can check, and the zero stays in the gradebook until you do.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Your own procedure has no deadline in it, so you're making one up. A deal I have to sign before I've seen a single page is exactly what I'll be describing to the principal. Show me the documents.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
Helping him means the zero comes off and nothing touches his record. You prove yourself wrong by putting the outline and the quotation in my hands. I'm waiting.
